minors, penalties.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers financial responsibility, which in practice means insurance. You must carry proof of financial responsibility whenever you drive and for drive tests, and you must show it to every driver involved in a collision. We will look at the minimum coverage amounts, who covers drivers under eighteen, how to check that an insurance seller is licensed, and what happens to a driver who is in a crash without insurance. That last rule surprises many people, because it applies even when the uninsured driver did nothing wrong in the crash itself.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The coverage minimums","fact_ids":["sec10-F02","sec10-F01","sec10-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Thirty thousand for one person.","fact_ids":["sec10-F02","sec10-F01","sec10-R01"]},{"text":"Sixty thousand for multiple victims.","fact_ids":["sec10-F02","sec10-F01","sec10-R01"]},{"text":"Fifteen thousand for property.","fact_ids":["sec10-F02","sec10-F01","sec10-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Minimum coverage runs thirty thousand dollars for the death or injury of one person, sixty thousand dollars for multiple victims, and fifteen thousand dollars for property damage. These three numbers form a staircase: one person, more than one person, and property. Carry proof of this coverage every time you drive and whenever you take a drive test, and show it to every driver involved after any collision. Learning the three amounts in order, thirty, sixty, and fifteen, makes it easier to match each one to what it covers when you see them on a question.","fact_ids":["sec10-F02","sec10-F01","sec10-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Minors, sellers and the uninsured","fact_ids":["sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Parents insure drivers under eighteen.","fact_ids":["sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-R01"]},{"text":"Check seller licensing.","fact_ids":["sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-R01"]},{"text":"Uninsured crash: up to four years.","fact_ids":["sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Parents and guardians cover drivers under eighteen and pay for their crash damages, while adults insure themselves. Buyers can verify that an agent, broker, or company is licensed through the state insurance department. A driver who is in a crash without insurance loses driving for up to four years, regardless of fault. They can win it back for the final three years by filing and keeping an SR twenty-two or SR one-P certificate, and drivers with low incomes may qualify for the state's low-cost auto insurance program. So proof rides along on every trip, and missing it can be very costly.","fact_ids":["sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Not my fault, no penalty?","fact_ids":["sec10-F04","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: fault decides the penalty.","fact_ids":["sec10-F04","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-R01"]},{"text":"Truth: uninsured penalties apply regardless.","fact_ids":["sec10-F04","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap. People assume that if another driver causes a crash, an uninsured driver who was hit faces no penalty. The handbook says uninsured crashers lose driving for up to four years regardless of fault. A second trap is mixing up the coverage minimums. Thirty thousand dollars covers the death or injury of one person, sixty thousand covers multiple victims, and fifteen thousand covers property damage. A third trap is assuming a young driver insures themselves; parents and guardians cover drivers under eighteen and pay their crash damages.","fact_ids":["sec10-F04","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check your understanding","fact_ids":["sec10-F02","sec10-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"One person is injured.","fact_ids":["sec10-F02","sec10-R01"]},{"text":"What is the minimum coverage?","fact_ids":["sec10-F02","sec10-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: what is the minimum coverage for the death or injury of one person? Decide on your answer. The answer is thirty thousand dollars. For multiple victims, the minimum is sixty thousand dollars, and for property damage it is fifteen thousand dollars. If you answered thirty thousand, you have the first step of the staircase. If you answered sixty thousand, you picked the multiple-victim amount. Keep them in order: thirty for one person, sixty for more than one, and fifteen for property, and carry proof of that coverage on every drive.","fact_ids":["sec10-F02","sec10-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u01-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Insurance recap","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Proof on every drive and test.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-R01"]},{"text":"Thirty, sixty, fifteen thousand.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up, carry proof of financial responsibility whenever you drive and for drive tests, and show it to every driver involved after a collision. The minimums are thirty thousand dollars for one death or injury, sixty thousand for multiple victims, and fifteen thousand for property damage. Parents and guardians cover drivers under eighteen, and buyers can check seller licensing through the state insurance department. A driver in a crash without insurance loses driving for up to four years regardless of fault, with SR twenty-two or SR one-P certificates and a low-cost program as paths back.","fact_ids":["sec10-F01","sec10-F02","sec10-F03","sec10-F04","sec10-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec10-u02","module_id":"sec10-m02","objective_ids":["sec10-u02"],"title":{"text":"Causes and duties at a crash","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-F06","sec10-F07"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Knowing the leading causes helps you avoid crashes, and knowing the scene duties keeps you within the law if one happens.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-F06"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Kai backs into a parked car in a lot and cannot find its owner.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Struck parked cars need an owner search or an attached note with your name, phone number and address, plus a report.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-R02"]},"result":{"text":"Kai leaves a note with his name, phone number and address on the car and reports the crash.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking you may leave a minor crash if no one is hurt.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06"]},"correction":{"text":"Every crash demands stopping, since leaving is hit-and-run with severe punishment.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-R02"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Stop, call, swap, report.","fact_ids":["sec10-R02"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"You hit a deer and it is injured. Should you move it?","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-R02"]},"answer":{"text":"No, call a humane society or an officer without moving it.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08"]},"rationale":{"text":"Hurt or killed animals need a humane society or officer call, without moving them.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-R02"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Before and after a crash","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"What causes crashes.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08"]},{"text":"What you must do at one.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers the leading causes of crashes and what you must do if you are in one. Most crashes come from a short list of driver errors, and knowing the list helps you avoid them. If a crash does happen, the law sets clear duties: stop, help the injured, exchange information, and report. We will also cover what to do when you hit a parked car or property, or an animal. The common thread at the scene is staying, helping, and sharing information, because leaving the scene of any crash is hit-and-run, which carries severe punishment.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Leading crash causes","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Distraction, unsafe speed, bad turns.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-R02"]},{"text":"Ignored right-of-way and signals.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-R02"]},{"text":"Pass crash scenes slowly.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"The leading causes of crashes are distractions, unsafe speed, improper turns, ignoring the right-of-way, ignoring signals and signs, driving on the wrong side of the road, and driving at a speed out of step with traffic. When you see flashers ahead at a crash, slow down and pass carefully. Rubbernecking, slowing to stare at a crash, only blocks rescuers and can cause another crash. So crash causes rank human errors from distraction through off-pace speed, and the right response to a crash ahead is to slow down, pass carefully, and keep the road clear for help.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"At the scene","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Always stop; leaving is hit-and-run.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-R02"]},{"text":"Call nine-one-one for the injured.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-R02"]},{"text":"No one hurt: move clear, then call.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Every crash demands that you stop. Leaving is hit-and-run, which carries severe punishment. Call nine-one-one for anyone who is hurt. If nobody is hurt, move clear of traffic before calling. Exchange your license, registration, insurance, and address with the other drivers, officers, and victims. Report any crash with injury or death to law enforcement within twenty-four hours, either yourself or through an agent, broker, or lawyer. So the scene duties stack stopping against hit-and-run penalties, then nine-one-one for the injured, then the document swap and the twenty-four-hour report.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Parked cars, property, animals","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Find the owner or leave a note.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-R02"]},{"text":"Report the crash.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-R02"]},{"text":"Call for hurt animals; do not move them.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"If you hit a parked car or other property, try to find the owner. If you cannot, attach a note with your name, phone number, and address, and report the crash. If you hit an animal and it is hurt or killed, call a humane society or an officer, and do not move the animal. These duties apply even when no other driver is present, because the owner still needs a way to reach you. Twenty-four-hour police reports, parked-property notes, and animal calls close out the scene, so nothing is left without a record or a contact.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"The quiet getaway","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-F08","sec10-F05","sec10-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: no one saw, so leave.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-F08","sec10-F05","sec10-R02"]},{"text":"Truth: stop; leaving is hit-and-run.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-F08","sec10-F05","sec10-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap. After a minor crash with no injuries, or after hitting a parked car with no one around, some drivers simply leave. Every crash demands stopping, and leaving is hit-and-run with severe punishment. For a parked car, find the owner or leave a note with your name, phone number, and address, then report the crash. A second trap is moving an injured animal. Call a humane society or an officer instead, without moving it. A third trap is slowing to stare at a crash you pass; rubbernecking only blocks rescuers.","fact_ids":["sec10-F06","sec10-F08","sec10-F05","sec10-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check your understanding","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"You hit a deer.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-R02"]},{"text":"Should you move it?","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: you hit a deer and it is injured. Should you move it off the road? Make your call. The answer is no. Call a humane society or an officer, and do not move the animal. The same scene rules apply as with any crash: you stop, and you make sure the right people are told. If you answered no, you have the animal rule. Keep it with the parked-car rule, which calls for finding the owner or leaving a note with your name, phone number, and address, followed by a report. Every crash demands stopping, and leaving is hit-and-run.","fact_ids":["sec10-F08","sec10-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u02-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Crash duties recap","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Stop, help, exchange, report.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R02"]},{"text":"Notes for parked cars; calls for animals.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"To sum up, the leading crash causes are distraction, unsafe speed, bad turns, ignored right-of-way, ignored signals and signs, wrong-side driving, and off-pace speed, and you pass crash scenes slowly without rubbernecking. At every crash, stop; leaving is hit-and-run. Call nine-one-one for the injured, or move clear first if no one is hurt. Exchange license, registration, insurance, and address, and report injury or death crashes to law enforcement within twenty-four hours. For parked cars, find the owner or leave a note and report it, and for hurt animals, call without moving them.","fact_ids":["sec10-F05","sec10-F06","sec10-F07","sec10-F08","sec10-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec10-u03","module_id":"sec10-m03","objective_ids":["sec10-u03"],"title":{"text":"Reporting crashes to DMV","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11"]},"why_how":[{"text":"A crash report to DMV is a separate duty from the police report, and skipping it can cost your license.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Rosa's crash causes more than one thousand dollars of damage and no injuries.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09"]},"reasoning":{"text":"DMV reports go out within ten days for crashes with over one thousand dollars in property damage or any injury or death.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-R03"]},"result":{"text":"Rosa files the SR one with DMV within ten days, even though no one was hurt.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking the officer at the scene files the DMV report for you.","fact_ids":["sec10-F10"]},"correction":{"text":"For a qualifying crash, each driver must arrange an SR one filing with DMV, personally or through a representative, regardless of fault; police do not file it for the driver.","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-R03"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Over a thousand or anyone hurt: ten days to file.","fact_ids":["sec10-R03"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Does a crash on private property need an SR one report?","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-R03"]},"answer":{"text":"Yes, a driver or representative files it even on private property.","fact_ids":["sec10-F10"]},"rationale":{"text":"The SR one is filed by every driver, at fault or not, even on private property.","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-R03"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec10-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"The report to DMV","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"A separate duty from police.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11"]},{"text":"Triggers, filers and records.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers reporting a crash to DMV. This is a separate duty from reporting an injury crash to law enforcement, and it has its own triggers and deadline. We will look at which crashes must be reported to DMV and how soon, who must file the SR one accident report, and how reported crashes reach your driver record. The rules are short, but they catch many drivers off guard, especially the rule that every driver must file, whether at fault or not, and the rule that officers at the scene do not file this report for you.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"When and who","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Within ten days.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-R03"]},{"text":"Over one thousand dollars or any injury.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-R03"]},{"text":"A driver or representative files the SR one.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"A report must go to DMV within ten days for any crash with over one thousand dollars in property damage, or with any injury or death, however minor. Each driver or a representative files the California SR one report with DMV, whether at fault or not, and even if the crash happened on private property. Officers do not file it for you, and drivers who skip it lose their driving. So DMV reporting fires on the thousand-dollar trigger and the any-injury trigger within ten days, with a driver or representative filing regardless of fault or who owns the pavement.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Crashes on your record","fact_ids":["sec10-F11","sec10-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Reported crashes land on records.","fact_ids":["sec10-F11","sec10-R03"]},{"text":"Regardless of fault.","fact_ids":["sec10-F11","sec10-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Reported crashes with over one thousand dollars of damage or any injury land on driver records, because of the duty to report, regardless of fault. That means a crash you did not cause can still appear on your record once it is reported. Records absorb every reported crash by driver duty alone. Put together with the earlier rules, the reporting picture is: ten days to file the SR one when the trigger is met, a driver or representative files it, officers file nothing for you, and the crash reaches your record whether or not you were at fault.","fact_ids":["sec10-F11","sec10-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u03-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"The officer has it covered","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-F09","sec10-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Trap: police file the DMV report.","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-F09","sec10-R03"]},{"text":"Truth: driver or representative files the SR one.","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-F09","sec10-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap. After a crash where police came to the scene, drivers often assume the officer's report takes care of DMV. It does not. Officers file nothing for you, and each driver must arrange SR one filing with DMV, personally or through a representative within ten days when the crash causes over one thousand dollars in damage or any injury or death. Skipping it costs your driving. A second trap is thinking a crash in a private parking lot does not count. The SR one is required even on private property, and it is required whether or not you were at fault. The report is due within ten days.","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-F09","sec10-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u03-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check your understanding","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-R03","sec10-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"A crash on private property.","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-R03","sec10-F09"]},{"text":"Is an SR one needed?","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-R03","sec10-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: does a crash on private property need an SR one report? Choose your answer. Yes. Each driver or a representative files the SR one with DMV, whether at fault or not, and even on private property, when the crash causes over one thousand dollars in damage or any injury or death. The report is due within ten days. If you answered yes, you have the rule. If you answered no, remember that the location of the crash does not change the duty, and that officers at the scene do not file this report for you. Drivers who skip the SR one lose their driving.","fact_ids":["sec10-F10","sec10-R03","sec10-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec10-u03-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Section wrap-up","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Ten days, over one thousand or any injury.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-R03"]},{"text":"Driver or representative files; records absorb it.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"To finish this section, report a crash to DMV within ten days when it causes over one thousand dollars in property damage or any injury or death, however minor. Each driver or a representative files the California SR one with DMV, at fault or not, even on private property, because officers file nothing and drivers who skip it lose their driving. Reported crashes land on driver records regardless of fault. Together with carrying proof of insurance and meeting the scene duties, these reporting rules complete what you must do about financial responsibility and collisions.","fact_ids":["sec10-F09","sec10-F10","sec10-F11","sec10-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]}]}
